Tiny is an offline-first teacher-support and family-engagement product for primary schools. Teachers use the app; parents use ordinary SMS; pupils have no accounts.
This hosted workspace contains sample records and a synthetic account. It is not connected to real children, guardians or SMS.
Sample data is stored in this browser. Local data is not encrypted; do not enter real personal information.
Remote writes are unavailable under the current zero-cost configuration.
Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo are complete draft translations awaiting native review. English remains the fallback.

Draft a short Primary 4 basic science lesson outline about sources and uses of water using the 5E structure. Use at most 140 English words.
Explain the water cycle in simple English for a Primary 4 teacher, with one local example. Use at most 100 words.
Suggest three ways to adapt a Primary 4 water lesson for pupils with mixed reading levels, using low-cost classroom materials. Use at most 120 English words.
Suggest a five-question quick check for understanding after a Primary 4 lesson on sources and uses of water. Include answers. Use at most 140 English words.
Suggest two practical ways a teacher can support a pupil who is still unsure about sources of water, without labelling or diagnosing the child. Use at most 100 English words.
Draft a short, factual, friendly family message about the week\'s water lesson and one home activity. Do not mention any pupil name, phone number, grade or diagnosis. Use at most 60 English words.
Chrome built-in AI requires a supported browser, the model, sufficient hardware and model download. This workspace does not claim on-device execution unless the SDK reports it.

How families use ordinary SMS: absence alerts, weekly updates, replies and consent.
This workspace does not send live SMS, deploy Cloud Functions, or claim cross-device sync. AI is optional; on-device Gemini Nano needs supported hardware. Sample records are used throughout.
Ask your school lead or the Tiny pilot contact for help with accounts, devices or privacy questions.
Choose your language, open your workspace and use Home for the next useful action. Everything you create is saved on this device first.
Open Classes, choose Add class, pick the grade, add a section label such as Blue, and save. You can teach more than one class and switch at any time.
Open a class, choose Add pupil and enter a display name. A local code is optional. Use sample records in this evaluation workspace, never real child data.
Add a guardian endpoint, link it to a pupil and record consent. One guardian may be linked to several pupils. Verify in person before any family message.
Open a class and choose Mark attendance. Mark every active pupil, save a draft if needed, then submit. Only absences can trigger an immediate message after server acceptance.
Open Lessons, create a draft and complete the objective, materials and five 5E stages. The plan is stored offline and remains available without a network.
Open a pupil from the roster, write a short factual observation and save a draft. Approve it before it can enter a family digest. Never use AI grading or diagnosis.
Open Messages to read family replies and queue a short response. A queued message is not a delivery confirmation. Guardian SMS is simulated here.
Choose what you need, generate an idea and review it. No pupil names or records are sent. If a model is unavailable, a reviewed offline strategy appears.
Classes, attendance, lessons, progress and drafts stay usable without a signal. The offline banner tells you when the device is disconnected.
The outbox shows what is saved and queued. Synced appears only after a real server acknowledgement. Server sync is unavailable in this zero-cost build.

If a screen looks empty, return to Home and reopen it. If sign-in fails, check the number or evaluation details. If AI is unavailable, use the offline library. Reset local sample data from Settings when needed.
Use synthetic records only in this workspace. Do not enter real pupil or guardian information. Local browser data is not encrypted; the Android app uses an encrypted database.
Guardians do not install Tiny and do not need an account. They receive and send ordinary SMS.
An absence alert arrives after the school register is accepted. Present and late do not trigger an immediate alert.
A weekly digest contains only approved, factual learning updates and school notices.
A guardian can reply to the school SMS. The teacher sees the reply in the family inbox.
STOP and START control consent. Unverified or ambiguous senders never receive child details.
A short walkthrough of the teacher workspace. You can leave at any time and replay it from Help.
Families use ordinary SMS. This short guide explains what they receive and how consent works.
Home shows today\'s classes, attendance status, queued work and unread family messages. Start with the next useful action.
Classes keeps every class and roster in one place. Open a class to see pupils, registers and lessons.
Inside a class, choose Add pupil and enter a display name. A short local code is optional. This evaluation uses sample records only.
Mark every active pupil present, absent or late. Save a draft or submit the register. Only absences can trigger an immediate family alert after server acceptance.
Create a teacher-authored 5E plan with objective, materials, Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate and Evaluate. Plans stay available offline.
Open a pupil and record a short factual observation. Approve it before it can enter a family digest. AI never grades or diagnoses a child.
The family inbox collects guardian SMS replies. Queue a short factual response. A queued reply is not a delivery confirmation.
The optional helper suggests lesson ideas, explanations, adaptations, checks and family-message drafts. Review everything; offline strategies always remain available.
Attendance, lessons, progress, classes and drafts work without a network. The offline banner appears when the connection drops.
The sync centre shows what is stored and queued. A synced state appears only after a real acknowledgement. No cloud write is claimed in this zero-cost build.
A guardian receives an SMS when a pupil is absent and the school register has been accepted. Present and late do not trigger an immediate alert.
On Friday afternoon, an approved digest can include factual learning updates and school notices. Nothing unapproved is shared.
A guardian can reply to the school SMS. The teacher reads it in the family inbox and can queue a response.
STOP and START control consent. Child details are never sent to unverified or ambiguous senders. This evaluation simulates SMS only.
